items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: She became the biggest soprano in Europe with Salomé and with many of these wonderful things.

ctx.x: Day-o. I did – the teachers were all doing – they were doing their whole acts, and I was in [the show] with the shirt tied around and . . . I chased everything. They told me who I could date, because I was single. They said I could date anybody who was a senior. Now at the colored schools at that time, particularly places like Lincoln and some of those schools, they had what they call sundown hours. The girls had to be in at sundown. You could not ride in a car unless you had permission. It was very, very…
She became the biggest soprano in Europe with Salomé and with many of these wonderful things.
